Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: ibn (or bin) Abi (or Abu) Jum'ah is a patronymic name, meaning "son of Abu Jum'ah" al-Maghrawi is a nisba, a name signifying place of origin or tribal affiliation. Devin J. Stewart, while agreeing that al-Maghrawi must be a toponymic, instead argued that it refers to Maghrawah, an area in north-western Algeria.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: While an opinion, argued by L. P. Harvey held that it means "of the _____ [tribe]"
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: Devin J. Stewart, while agreeing that al-Maghrawi must be a toponymic, instead argued that it refers to Maghrawah, an area in north-western Algeria. While an opinion, argued by L. P. Harvey held that it means "of the Maghrawa [tribe]".

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: al-_____ is another nisba, which means "of Oran", referring to the city of Oran (Arabic: وهران, Wahran) in Western Algeria
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: al-Wahrani is another nisba, which means "of Oran", referring to the city of Oran (Arabic: وهران, Wahran) in Western Algeria. The renditions that appeared include: "Ahmed ben Juma'a", "Ubaydallah Ahmed Ben Bu Jumu'ah", "Ahmad fijo de Abu Jumu'ah", "Obaydala Ahmed Abenabigiomoa", "Ubayd Allah al-Wahrani" and "Ahmad Bu Jum'a".

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: In some of the manuscripts the name "_____" is also added, a theophoric name that means "the little servant of God", and was likely added as a pious formula
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: In some of the manuscripts the name "Ubaydallah" is also added, a theophoric name that means "the little servant of God", and was likely added as a pious formula. The renditions that appeared include: "Ahmed ben Juma'a", "Ubaydallah Ahmed Ben Bu Jumu'ah", "Ahmad fijo de Abu Jumu'ah", "Obaydala Ahmed Abenabigiomoa", "Ubayd Allah al-Wahrani" and "Ahmad Bu Jum'a".

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: The renditions that appeared include: "Ahmed ben Juma'a", "_____'ah", "Ahmad fijo de Abu Jumu'ah", "Obaydala Ahmed Abenabigiomoa", "Ubayd Allah al-Wahrani" and "Ahmad Bu Jum'a"
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: The renditions that appeared include: "Ahmed ben Juma'a", "Ubaydallah Ahmed Ben Bu Jumu'ah", "Ahmad fijo de Abu Jumu'ah", "Obaydala Ahmed Abenabigiomoa", "Ubayd Allah al-Wahrani" and "Ahmad Bu Jum'a".

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: He may have been born in Oran, then part of the _____ kingdom of Tlemcen, or in the nearby region of Maghrawah
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: He may have been born in Oran, then part of the Zayyanid kingdom of Tlemcen, or in the nearby region of Maghrawah.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: In either way, he was presumably of Berber origin and belonged to the _____ tribal confederation
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: He may have been born in Oran, then part of the Zayyanid kingdom of Tlemcen, or in the nearby region of Maghrawah. In either way, he was presumably of Berber origin and belonged to the Maghrawah tribal confederation.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: Some opinions also say that he was a native of Spain, born in _____
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: Some opinions also say that he was a native of Spain, born in Almagro.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: He studied in Oran in his early years, then moved to _____, the nearest major capital to get an education in Islamic law and theology
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: He studied in Oran in his early years, then moved to Tlemcen, the nearest major capital to get an education in Islamic law and theology. In Tlemcen he wrote Jami' Jawami' al-Ikhtisar wa al-Tibyan and had a teaching position.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: He studied under _____ ibn Yusuf al-Sanusi, a well-known Islamic scholar
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: He studied under Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Sanusi, a well-known Islamic scholar.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: In Tlemcen he wrote Jami' _____' al-Ikhtisar wa al-Tibyan and had a teaching position
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: In Tlemcen he wrote Jami' Jawami' al-Ikhtisar wa al-Tibyan and had a teaching position.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: At some point (estimated to be around _____), he moved to Fez and obtained a salaried position as a professor of law
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: At some point (estimated to be around 1493), he moved to Fez and obtained a salaried position as a professor of law.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: He issued the Oran fatwa in _____, likely when he was in Fez
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: He issued the Oran fatwa in 1504, likely when he was in Fez.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: He died in Fez in 3 June _____
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: He died in Fez in 3 June 1511.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: His son, _____ would also become an Islamic scholar
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: His son, Muhammad Shaqrun would also become an Islamic scholar.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: Because of his authorship of the _____ fatwa, he has frequently been referred to as "the Mufti of Oran", suggesting that he wrote the fatwa there and he had some sort of official authority as a mufti
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: He was identified as the author of the 1504 fatwa commonly named the Oran fatwa, instructing the Muslims in Spain about how to secretly practice Islam, and granting comprehensive dispensations for them to publicly conform to Christianity and performing acts normally forbidden in Islam when necessary to survive. Because of his authorship of the fatwa he is often called "the Mufti of Oran", although he likely issued the fatwa in Fez, not in Oran and he did not have any official capacity in eith...

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: However, _____ noted that he was active in Fez (in today's Morocco), not Oran, at the time of the fatwa's composition, and likely penned it there
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: However, Devin J. Stewart noted that he was active in Fez (in today's Morocco), not Oran, at the time of the fatwa's composition, and likely penned it there.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: In theory, any competent _____ jurist could issue a fatwa, although normally it carries less weight than ones from an official mufti
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: In theory, any competent Islamic jurist could issue a fatwa, although normally it carries less weight than ones from an official mufti.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: The name "Oran fatwa" itself was given by modern scholars due to the name al-_____ ("of Oran") that appeared in the text as part of his name
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: The name "Oran fatwa" itself was given by modern scholars due to the name al-Wahrani ("of Oran") that appeared in the text as part of his name.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: The fatwa, while reaffirming the orthodox obligation of all _____, sets out detailed relaxations of the sharia requirements for the benefit of the persecuted Muslims of Spain
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: The fatwa instructed the Muslims in Spain about how to secretly practice Islam, and granted comprehensive dispensations for them to publicly conform to Christianity and perform acts normally forbidden in Islam when necessary to survive. The fatwa, while reaffirming the orthodox obligation of all Muslims, sets out detailed relaxations of the sharia requirements for the benefit of the persecuted Muslims of Spain.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: The fatwa enjoyed wide currency among Muslims and Moriscos (Muslims nominally converted to Christianity and their descendants) in Spain, and one of the surviving aljamiado translations was dated at __
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: The fatwa enjoyed wide currency among Muslims and Moriscos (Muslims nominally converted to Christianity and their descendants) in Spain, and one of the surviving aljamiado translations was dated at 1564, 60 years after the original fatwa.

Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.question: The fatwa has been described as the "key theological document" to understand the practice of _____ following the Reconquista up to the expulsion of the Moriscos
Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah.fact: The fatwa has been described as the "key theological document" to understand the practice of Spanish Muslims following the Reconquista up to the expulsion of the Moriscos.

Ahmed Harrak Srifi.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmed Harrak Srifi.question: The _____ was Moroccan academic.
Ahmed Harrak Srifi.fact: Ahmed Harrak Srifi (Arabic: أحمد الحراق السريفي) was a prominent Moroccan scholar from the tribe of Ahl Srif in the north of Morocco.

Ahmed Harrak Srifi.subject: Indian Festivals & Fairs
Ahmed Harrak Srifi.question: As a _____ theologian, he specialized in the study of the Quran and of Hadith narration with regard to different interesting of the Quran
Ahmed Harrak Srifi.fact: As a Muslim theologian, he specialized in the study of the Quran and of Hadith narration with regard to different interesting of the Quran.
